extracted.intended_audience: Macaulay2 package authors and Macaulay2 documentation contributors (programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing documentation entries for Macaulay2 packages and the Macaulay2 system, including required placement, available formats, style conventions, and the edit/generate/review cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation for user defined packages and Macaulay2 itself is written using two main methods: the document(List) function, using a list-based hypertext markup format; the doc(String) function, using a string-based SimpleDoc format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one of these two supported methods when authoring documentation so it will be formatted correctly for installPackage, online HTML, and info pages. See the pages for each method for templates and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation must be part of a package and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each documentation entry must be part of a package, and occur after the beginDocumentation section of the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your documentation nodes are placed in the package source after beginDocumentation so the build tools (installPackage) will pick them up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of documentation entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Each documentation entry is either an overview topic, or documentation of an individual feature, such as a symbol, a function name, a function call (that is, a function name, together with specific types of its arguments), an optional argument to a function, or a package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate entry type when creating a node (overview vs feature vs call/argument) so users can find the right granularity of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start from examples/templates
rubrics_metrics.description: The easiest way to write documentation for an entry is to start with an example as a template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided templates and example entries (see the documentation on document and doc) as starting points and adapt them rather than writing from scratch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation editing cycle (edit → build → review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cycle: Edit your documentation entries as desired; Generate the html pages for your package, using installPackage("YourPackage"); Review the generated HTML documentation using viewHelp which displays this page in a browser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iteratively refine documentation by repeating edit → installPackage → viewHelp until the rendered output meets quality expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of TO for hyperlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use TO to reference any Macaulay2 function, option, or variable occurring in the documentation as a hyperlink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark function/option/variable names with the TO markup so that documentation generation produces hyperlinks to the corresponding nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title capitalization convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Lowercase is used for all titles, unless a proper noun is being used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer all-lowercase titles for documentation nodes (capitalize only proper nouns) to maintain a consistent style across the documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation for Inputs / Outputs / Consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Inputs, Outputs, and Consequences should not end with periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing these standardized sections, omit terminal periods to follow the project's stylistic convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include standard documentation keys/sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standardized keys/sections such as See also, EXAMPLE, SYNOPSIS, and other documentation keys (document, tutorial, undocumented, ofClass, EXAMPLE, SYNOPSIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ the canonical section names (e.g., EXAMPLE for constructing hypertext items, SYNOPSIS for a standardized synopsis) so that readers and tools can rely on consistent structure; consult the documentation keys list for meanings and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate documentation formats via installPackage
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation is formatted via installPackage as the documentation built into Macaulay2, the online HTML documentation, and the info pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use installPackage to produce the various output formats (built-in help, HTML, info pages) and check that all formats render correctly during your review cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation is automatically structured
rubrics_metrics.description: Much of the format and structure of the documentation is automatically generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage the automatic structuring provided by the documentation system; focus on content and correct use of markup so the generator can produce coherent pages.
